races.name: QuinnBet Apprentice Optional Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with modest recent form (8 from last six runs) who is a genuine hold-up horse operating on Good going within OR range, but the congested midfield mapping masks a style that needs a strongly-run race to land a blow — 12 days between runs is fine but the pace scenario here does not obviously suit.

runners_data.name: Kakori
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old for JP O'Brien returning after 69 days, which is the biggest fitness flag in the field; races from the rear and will need this 10f trip to really develop a strong gallop for his hold-up style to function, with Good ground suiting on the evidence.

runners_data.name: Loingseoir
runners_data.note: Consistent ten-year-old veteran who has placed nine times from 15 similar-going runs including a win, handles Good ground well and is genuine at the trip; Jack Cleary takes 2lbs off, and the horse's proximity racing style means he could travel in the second tier without being fully compromised by the hold-up traffic.

runners_data.name: Phidias Ovation
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish flag and sits on OR=53 as the lowest-rated runner; returning from 67 days off for a small trainer without recent runners (T14: 0/0), and a natural closer who has failed to trouble the judge on Good ground across five recent runs — the redistribution to midfield compounds an already difficult task.

runners_data.name: Bucaneer's Spirit
runners_data.note: Strong record on Good turf (12 from 15 sim-going runs, 1W4P) and a genuine hold-up performer who has placed at this sort of trip and going combination before; 21 days between runs is fine, and if any of the true closers can make ground from a compressed midfield this is the one with the consistency profile to do it.

runners_data.name: Kashel Spring
runners_data.note: Handicap mark of OR=73 makes her the top-rated runner and she carries 7lb claimer Mel Sheridan; recent form includes placed efforts at 10f and 12f on Good, but her last three runs on soft or heavy have been poor — Good ground is clearly needed and she gets it here, though her hold-up tendencies put her in a tricky tactical spot.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner — won at 10f on Good going and has course-relevant form; T14 strike-rate is modest at 1/24 for Hogan but the horse's role as sole pace-setter is the key asset, and the 11-day turnaround is not a concern given recent racecourse fitness.

runners_data.name: Concert Party
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old with no wins and a flat recent form string (0/0 placed from last six); mapped to midfield from a true hold-up role, and with OR=64 on the second-lightest weight in the field the apprentice's 7lb claim is relevant, but the form offers no platform for confidence in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Forlio
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Good going and has placed multiple times at distance — the combination of genuine hold-up style, Good ground, and experience at the trip makes this one of the more credible back-half horses; 10 days since last run is fine, and the 2lb claim from Nicola Burns adds marginal value.

runners_data.name: Moyassr
runners_data.note: Compact form (1W1P from 15 sim-going runs) with the most recent win at 10f on Good — genuinely holds up but is being mapped to midfield due to the congested closer traffic; the OR=63 suggests he may need a very specific race shape, and Paul Flynn's stable is at 0/27 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: She's Ideal
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 10f on Good going are directly relevant to this trip and surface; prominent style means she is one of only two horses naturally suited to tracking the pace, apprentice McGettigan claims 2lbs, and the six-day turnaround for McGuinness (5/28, T14) suggests the trainer is confident she is ready to go again.

races.paceDynamic: Hexagonal is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in this 11-runner field, she will dictate from the front at a pace of her own choosing over this flat 1m2½f Roscommon trip on Good ground. She's Ideal is the only other horse with a prominent style and will press or track Hexagonal closely, meaning the early tempo is likely to be honest but controlled rather than truly searching. The back-half of the field is saturated with hold-up types — Darkdeserthighway, Kakori, Bucaneer's Spirit, Concert Party, Phidias Ovation and Moyassr are all genuine closers compressed into midfield on the map because there are more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, and most will not run as freely as they would in a smaller, less congested field. This controlled, front-two-dominated shape strongly favours runners who can travel prominently with cover and produce a sustained finish — horses with prominent or forward-tracking profiles will be best placed to exploit an even tempo that does not stretch the field early, while true hold-up horses face a traffic puzzle and a pace insufficient to set up a late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hexagonal Controls Freely
scenarios.trigger: If Hexagonal leads unchallenged through a steady-honest gallop and She's Ideal tracks in second.
scenarios.body: Hexagonal dictates the tempo from flag to finish on her favoured Good ground and comes off the turn with a clear advantage, making it a test of stamina and tactical speed rather than raw finishing pace; She's Ideal, travelling prominently in her wheel, is ideally positioned to challenge if Hexagonal flattens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If She's Ideal times a challenge to perfection turning in and Hexagonal's front-running effort compounds in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: She's Ideal has won twice over 10f on Good going and her apprentice claims an allowance; travelling in the slipstream of a lone setter on a flat track is her optimal scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Split Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the field strings out, enabling the best-credentialled hold-up horses to motor through.
scenarios.body: Bucaneer's Spirit and Forlio both carry form on Good turf over similar trips and could pick off tiring rivals if the early fractions prove more honest than anticipated; both are genuine hold-up performers — unlike several redistibuted midfielders — and would be the most likely beneficiaries if the race develops a true strong gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Hexagonal sets a crawl and the race turns into a sprint for home with little meaningful tempo.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race compresses the field and reduces the advantage of positional runners, but in that scenario a horse with a sharp turn of foot and good position like She's Ideal still benefits; Loingseoir, consistent on Good going with multiple placed efforts, could emerge from midfield if the sprint suits his profile at the trip.

watchPoints.text: Hexagonal's early gallop is the axis of the whole race — watch whether She's Ideal pushes alongside and forces a quicker pace or settles in behind, as that decision in the first two furlongs dictates whether front-runners or closers are favoured.

Bucaneer's Spirit and Forlio are the two most credible hold-up horses in the field but will need the traffic on the turn to clear — if they are boxed in at the bend they lose their moment even in a scenario where the pace suits them.

Kakori's 69-day absence is the longest layoff in the field and JP O'Brien's 14-day return rate is 6/55 — watch market moves as a significant gamble would suggest the stable is confident, otherwise treat the fitness query as live.

Kashel Spring carries the highest OR but her last three runs on non-Good ground have been well below form; she needs the Going Report's confirmed Good to run to her rating and is worth watching in the betting for any drift that suggests connections have reservations.

The 7lb claim from apprentice Mel Sheridan on Kashel Spring and the 7lb claim from Jared Huggan on Concert Party are both significant weight reductions — watch whether either horse attracts late market support that implies their connections expect the apprentice allowance to be a material factor in a moderate-OR field.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Captain James Cook
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for the powerful A.P. O'Brien/Wayne Lordan combination, stepping up to 7½f having shown modest form over 6f on good ground; the extra distance may suit and a prominent pitch keeps him in contention if Nando Royale is caught.|

runners_data.name: Eighteenth Smiles
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle rides for Joseph Patrick O'Brien and the horse carries headgear (p); a genuine rear-of-field operator by instinct, it will need to overcome the compressed race shape where the lone front-runner sets a forgiving tempo unfavourable to late finishers.|

runners_data.name: Hypiradon
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Kevin Coleman who has twice finished in the rear half over 7f on good ground; with no strong pace to close into, the race is likely to be over before Rory Cleary can mount a challenge from off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Nando Royale
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Gavin Cromwell and Gary Carroll, holding a career placed effort and clear experience over similar trips on good ground — the key horse to watch as the lone leader who sets the race's entire tempo and shape.|

runners_data.name: Pints Of Glory
runners_data.note: Colin Keane rides this G.M. Lyons-trained hold-up type stepping back from 8f; finished fourth last time so possesses a modicum of form, and if the pace is stronger than expected, Keane's positional awareness gives this a slim chance of benefiting.|

runners_data.name: Prince Of Peppard
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this J.P. Murtagh hold-up runner who has finished sixth and ninth over 6f on good ground; limited form to date and racing from the rear into a tempo that is unlikely to quicken enough to bring hold-up horses into play.|

runners_data.name: Cashel Queen
runners_data.note: Donnacha Aidan O'Brien's filly has placed form (2nd, 3rd) over 7-8f and arrives on a 32-day break with apprentice Paddy Harnett claiming 5lb; naturally wants to come from behind but finds herself in a race shape mapped to midfield, which constrains her true finishing style.|

runners_data.name: Green Sparkle
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's runner showed a tendency to fade in the finish and has run tenth and ninth over 7f on good ground — a genuine hold-up type who, because of the surplus of rear-runners in this field, will race in a more forward position than ideal, compounding an already modest recent profile.|

runners_data.name: Honey Deuce
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the ride for J.A. Stack on this hold-up type who finished sixth and ninth over 7f; only one run on strictly good ground and with no strong pace to chase down, this remains a difficult winning chance from the back.|

runners_data.name: Luca Brillante
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unclassified stylistically by the pace model, Chris Hayes rides for D.K. Weld who has only one runner in the past 14 days; seventh and sixth over 6f suggest gradual improvement is possible but the step to 7½f is untested.|

runners_data.name: Matavai Bay
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this Kevin Coleman prominent runner who has bumped into the rear on both starts over 6-7f; stepping up in distance could help and racing close to Nando Royale is the only tactical avenue available to a horse with this profile.|

runners_data.name: Someday Somewhere
runners_data.note: W.J. Lee rides this lightly raced, unclassified type for Stephen Thorne who has no runners in the past 14 days; placed form (third, fourth) over 6-7f on good ground suggests competence and the unknown style profile means any position is possible — a genuine wild card.|

races.paceDynamic: Nando Royale is the confirmed and likely sole front-runner in this 12-runner 7½f maiden on good ground at Roscommon, and with no meaningful challenger for the lead, Gary Carroll can dictate a comfortable, controlled tempo from the front without being pressured at any stage. Captain James Cook and Matavai Bay are the natural prominent horses and will likely settle in behind Nando Royale, creating a compact early order with the bulk of the field strung out through midfield. With a sustainable, uncontested gallop expected, the race is set up squarely to favour those who can race prominently and kick off a steady pace — hold-up horses will face an awkward task as the tempo is unlikely to be generous enough for them to reel in the leader late. Several genuine hold-up types — Green Sparkle, Cashel Queen, and Eighteenth Smiles — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because this field holds more horses with rear-of-field instincts than can realistically find space at the back; in practice Nando Royale and the two genuine prominent racers are most likely to secure their natural positions, while the redistributed trio will need to overcome an unfavourable race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nando Royale controls unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Nando Royale leads comfortably throughout and the pace stays honest without acceleration, rewarding those on or near the pace.
scenarios.body: Carroll dictates every stride from the front and the field strings out behind at a rhythm that suits gallopers rather than finishers; horses who can travel prominently into the straight without burning energy have the decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent pair pounce late on leader
scenarios.trigger: If Nando Royale's lead is reeled in from the two-furlong mark by Captain James Cook or Matavai Bay coming with a sustained run from behind the pace.
scenarios.body: The early pace, though controlled, leaves enough in the tank for the closest pursuers to close strongly once the flat Roscommon straight opens up; this shape rewards horses who have settled just off the leader and quicken with a clear run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, midfield sweeper wins
scenarios.trigger: If Nando Royale burns out early or an unexpected injection of early pace causes the lead group to fold, handing momentum to a fresh horse from mid-division.
scenarios.body: A collapse of the front-running shape would allow a horse travelling comfortably in the mid-pack to pick off weakening rivals through the final two furlongs; Someday Somewhere and Pints Of Glory, if settled in range, are the likeliest beneficiaries of such a scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers pounce from rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out far enough to allow genuine hold-up horses to make late ground.
scenarios.body: This is structurally the least likely shape given the single front-runner and controlled tempo expected; Green Sparkle, Cashel Queen and Eighteenth Smiles are redistributed types not guaranteed their natural position, and their STYLE_FIT discount means this outcome relies on events that the pace map makes improbable.

watchPoints.text: Nando Royale's fractions in the first two furlongs are the single biggest determinant of this race — if Carroll settles into a genuinely unhurried lead, the race is almost certainly his to lose, and all other outcomes hinge on how comfortably he controls the pace.

Captain James Cook for Wayne Lordan and A.P. O'Brien bears close watching in the early stages — if Lordan slots him directly onto Nando Royale's quarters and travels without cover, he is the most likely horse to pounce on the leader in the straight.

Green Sparkle's tendency to fade in the finish is a key concern — mapped to midfield rather than its natural hold-up berth, Declan McDonogh will need to manage energy carefully or risk the horse weakening at the exact point the race is decided.

Someday Somewhere and Luca Brillante are both lightly raced with unknown style profiles — either could take up an unexpected position in running that alters the tactical picture, particularly if one of them elects to press Nando Royale early.

Cashel Queen's combination of placed form over the right trip and a 5lb claimer in Paddy Harnett is worth monitoring in the market — if confidence builds on course, she may move closer to the pace than her redistribution mapping suggests.

races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Race

runners_data.name: Seven Nation Army
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner with a recent course-relevant win over 7f on soft, but Roscommon's good ground is a slight concern given sim-going record of 0 wins from 1 on good; McDonogh will be quick from the gate but faces a direct pace rival in Sword Of State.

runners_data.name: Green Dreamer
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's stable is firing (6/55 in 14 days) and Dylan Browne McMonagle rides a horse with a useful 1-2-1 record over 8f on good; steps back in trip slightly but the prominent style suits a genuinely honest pace and this yard wins with well-prepared juveniles.

runners_data.name: Noble Agenda
runners_data.note: Won on sole start over 7f on soft for Ciaran Murphy, returning after 60 days which is the longest absence in the field — freshness could be an asset or a risk; Ben Coen is an intelligent tactician who will slot this prominent-style runner into a position to exploit a contested pace.

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: Busy juvenile with six career runs who has been placed four times but yet to win on good ground specifically (best form on yielding/soft or heavy); Wesley Joyce claims 3lb and will attempt to get cover from a prominent berth, but the ground-form mismatch is a concern.

runners_data.name: Oristown Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with an encouraging recent win over 7f on good and Rory Mulligan (5) in the saddle; the small trainer (0/3 in 14 days) is a risk factor but the horse's style is perfectly suited to benefit from a pace duel up front, provided a clear run materialises in the straight.

runners_data.name: Emotional Hedging
runners_data.note: Ran a fine second on debut over 6f on good for Gavin Cromwell (4/16 in 14 days — yard in form); Gary Carroll will look to deploy the prominent style just behind the leaders, and stepping to 7½f is an interesting stamina test for a horse who was doing her best work late at 6f.

runners_data.name: Grit And Glory
runners_data.note: Tagged with a fade-in-finish flag and sole run produced a distant 12th over 7f on good — no evidence yet of the ability to sustain a late challenge; Luke McAteer will need significant improvement from this Jack Foley-trained juvenile just to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Sword Of State
runners_data.note: Won last time over 7f on good and is a confirmed front-runner who will battle Seven Nation Army for the lead; Rory Cleary rides and the horse has finished 1-7 over 7f on good — the front-running style suits if it can shake off its rival, but the pace contest is the central risk.

runners_data.name: Gabby Hayes
runners_data.note: Sole run produced a remote ninth over 7f on good for Noel Meade (0/17 in 14 days — yard out of form) and the horse is flagged as fading in finishes; Chris Hayes takes the ride but there is no evidence of the ability needed to reverse that debut form in stronger company.

races.paceDynamic: Seven Nation Army and Sword Of State will both look to lead from the gates, creating a genuine pace duel over the opening two furlongs of this 7½f Roscommon contest on good ground. Lars Soldier and Green Dreamer add to the prominent cluster, meaning four of nine runners will be jostling for the first two or three positions — traffic interference between the two-furlong and three-furlong poles is a real danger for those caught wide or shuffled back. With two genuine front-runners pressing each other on good ground, the gallop is unlikely to be truly soft, producing an honest pace that will stretch the field and expose any stamina questions late. This race shape most favours hold-up horses with a clean late run, particularly those with proven form over 7f on good ground who can exploit a strong pace set by the duelling leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Seven Nation Army and Sword Of State press each other hard through the first three furlongs, leaving the prominent cluster to race in congested traffic.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will empty the pace-setters late, and any horse tracking smoothly in fourth or fifth with cover will sprint clear in the final furlong; good ground suits a fluent, well-paced closer who doesn't need to make their own running.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Conserves
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent horses (Green Dreamer, Noble Agenda, Emotional Hedging) slots in smoothly just off the duelling leaders and avoids traffic.
scenarios.body: With the front two fighting each other, a well-positioned prominent runner sits in behind them and produces a strong neck-and-neck finish in the final 1½f; Noble Agenda's unbeaten profile and Ben Coen's positioning ability make this credible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of Seven Nation Army or Sword Of State surges clear early and the other drops away, leaving an uncontested leader.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner on good ground at Roscommon over 7½f with a comfortable lead can dictate and coast home, as the hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is exceptionally fierce and the entire prominent group fades, allowing true hold-up horses to pick through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: Gabby Hayes and Grit And Glory would need the race to collapse in front of them, but both carry fade-in-finish flags and have failed to show the required punch in prior form.

watchPoints.text: Seven Nation Army and Sword Of State will lock horns for the lead from the start — watch the first two furlongs for which one blinks first, as the loser of that battle may drop out of contention quickly.

Lars Soldier, Green Dreamer, Noble Agenda, and Emotional Hedging all want prominent positions in a nine-runner field — traffic bunching between the 3f and 2f poles is highly likely and any rider caught wide without cover risks burning energy at the wrong moment.
Noble Agenda returns after 60 days off and has only the one run to her name — watch for signs of ring-rustiness early, particularly in a race that will be brisk from the outset.

Oristown Boy's hold-up style is well-suited to the pace shape but Rory Mulligan (5) must find a clean passage off the final bend — if trapped behind the prominent cluster, the straight at Roscommon is short enough to deny a late challenge.

Good ground has been consistent all card at Roscommon today, confirming no bias concern — horses with proven good-ground form (Sword Of State, Green Dreamer, Oristown Boy) are at no disadvantage relative to their form lines.

races.name: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Fillies Maiden
WTW Willis Handicap

runners_data.name: Engines On
runners_data.note: Prominent-running six-year-old who won over 7f on good ground last year and ran a respectable third 65 days ago; the step back to good ground suits (9/15 on similar) and the tongue-tie is retained, though the layoff since that run is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Summer Island
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Dylan Browne McMonagle who arrives in good form with two wins from the last five outings including a 7f success on good ground; only nine days since last run is no concern given recent profile, and the step up to 7½f looks a positive.

runners_data.name: Earls
runners_data.note: Consistent nine-year-old prominent racer for Gary Carroll and Gavin Cromwell who has placed in four of his last five starts, all at 8f on good to soft ground; the drop back to 7½f may be fractionally sharp, but strong trainer form (4/16 in 14 days) is a live angle.

runners_data.name: Spodo Komodo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will be first to post going on; won over 6f on soft and placed at 7f on good, but the three-way pace battle makes it very hard for him to last home over 7½f, and his OR of 78 reflects a horse who needs things his own way.

runners_data.name: Tokyo Treasure
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has placed three times in five runs on good ground at 7f; a 5lb claimer in the saddle lightens the weight burden, and a recent second over this exact trip on good ground is an obvious positive form line.

runners_data.name: Dragon Of Malta
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for a 7lb claimer who has shown quiet form at 7-8f on good ground recently; the age (nine) and modest trainer strike rate at OR=75 temper enthusiasm, but the good-ground profile (8/15) is solid and a low-key tactical ride could suit.

runners_data.name: Mehman
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who wears a hood and has a modest recent string including a third over 6f on good ground; the pattern of good-ground form (3/15 on similar going) is uninspiring, and the 7½f trip is longer than his recent winning distance of 6f.

runners_data.name: Red Hugh O'Donnell
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose form figures include a fourth and a fifth at 7-8f on good ground; tongue-tie and cheekpieces are retained, and the strong course-going stat (11/15) is the most interesting figure in his profile, though a 5lb claimer rides.

runners_data.name: Thenandnow
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer for Shane Foley and Mrs Harrington who finished third over 7f on good ground last time; stepping up from 6-7f to 7½f for the first time, and the big Harrington string (2/32 in 14 days) provides limited support, but Foley's booking is the key angle.

runners_data.name: Cool Azul
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 6f on good ground last time out for A. Oliver, who is firing (4/19 in 14 days); the jump from 6f to 7½f is a significant stamina question on breeding and form, and he must lead or get a lead — only two runs on similar going.

runners_data.name: Dolly Hello
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a solid run of placed efforts at 7-8f on good ground for Seamie Heffernan; 35 days since last run is not a concern given previous gap, and a third at 8f on good last time is the most encouraging line in a competitive career record.

runners_data.name: Contrary To Law
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent racer for Ben Coen and J.P. Murtagh who won over 7f on good ground and has placed at this trip previously; trainer sends two from 27 runners recently which is modest, but the good-ground profile and Coen booking are strong positives.

runners_data.name: Perfect Base
runners_data.note: Prominent type who wears a hood and whose recent form includes a second at 7f on good; 61 days off the track is the primary concern, and a return of 6/6 on good ground is reassuring, though the OR drop to 70 suggests connections have had to wait for a winnable opportunity.

runners_data.name: Venetian Star
runners_data.note: One of the three confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead; record includes two thirds at 7f on good ground, but the pace battle makes it extremely hard for him to win from the front, and his stepping-down OR of 74 reflects a horse yet to win at this level.

runners_data.name: Sagasti
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a visor retained, booked for Colin Keane which is the headline angle; form includes a second at 7f on standard and a third on good, but the pattern of wide draws and late fades on good ground (only 4/8 on similar) makes the booking more intriguing than the form.

runners_data.name: Mercurial
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who is genuinely a prominent racer but faces more pace rivals than can all secure a forward berth; with 79 days off the track for John J Nallen (0/4 in 14 days), the stable form dampens any optimism, and the redistribution into midfield is against his natural style.

runners_data.name: Java Wood
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer who will likely find himself further forward than ideal given the pace dynamics compressing the field; recent form includes a win at 8f on good and a third over 10f, suggesting the 7½f trip may be on the short side, and Reserve 2 in the saddle is an unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who carries a visor and arrives on the back of a string of placed efforts at 6-7f on good and soft; trainer Adrian McGuinness is in strong form (5/28 in 14 days), but with 15 days since last run and a Reserve 3 jockey, the positives are tactical rather than form-based, and racing out of his natural rear position is a complication.

races.paceDynamic: Spodo Komodo, Cool Azul, and Venetian Star are all confirmed front-runners in an 18-runner handicap over 7½f at Roscommon, meaning a genuine, unrelenting gallop from the outset is virtually certain — none of these three will concede the lead willingly, and the resulting friction will ensure fractions are honest throughout. With the pace battle likely to burn off the principals from the front, this race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently just off the pace or attack from midfield, preserving energy through the early stages before hitting the rising Roscommon finish with something left in reserve. Horses such as Engines On, Earls, Thenandnow, Tokyo Treasure, and Contrary To Law — who can slot just behind the carnage — are the primary beneficiaries of this shape. The field also contains more genuine prominent types than can all secure that position: Mercurial is a natural prominent racer who is most likely to get bumped back into midfield, while Java Wood and Flaming Rib are true hold-up horses who may find themselves further forward than ideal given the squeeze behind the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Spodo Komodo, Cool Azul, and Venetian Star fight for position and set a fast, sustained gallop that destroys them all in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace drains the front-runners, and the race becomes a stamina test that rewards horses travelling smoothly in the slipstream through the first half of the race; prominent types just off the duelling leaders get the ideal tow into contention. Engines On, Earls, and Summer Island are best positioned to capitalise as they possess the tactical speed to sit close enough to pounce once the leaders crack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Cool Azul or Spodo Komodo breaks smartly and establishes a clear lead while the others are slow away, dictating a controlled but honest gallop.
scenarios.body: With a single pace-setter able to dictate rhythm, the fractions become more manageable for the leader and a prominent horse that can shadow them unchallenged; this scenario shortens the relative advantage of deep closers. Cool Azul, who has shown a clean early pace and won last time, and Tokyo Treasure, who has the right profile to sit just off one leader, become live players in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other out faster than expected and the pace is so strong that even the prominent horses get flattened, opening the race up for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A truly ruinous early pace could stretch the field and leave a clear lane on the outside in the straight for those held up; Summer Island, who has strong form at both 7f and 8f on good ground, and Dragon Of Malta, who has shown the ability to close well over this trip, are the best-equipped genuine hold-up horses. Note that Java Wood and Flaming Rib, true closers who have been mapped further forward than their natural style, are less likely to fulfil the closer role cleanly in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not catastrophic, producing a strung-out race that rewards a horse with a high cruising speed from midfield who never has to change gears sharply.
scenarios.body: In this shape the race settles into a rhythm that suits horses comfortable travelling in the middle third of the field with the ability to sustain their effort through the final two furlongs rather than produce a single burst; Contrary To Law and Thenandnow, both with versatile profiles and decent recent form on good ground at this trip, fit the bill. Sagasti under Colin Keane has the booking to suggest connections believe this shape could emerge, though the horse's recent form has been inconsistent.

watchPoints.text: Spodo Komodo, Cool Azul, and Venetian Star will all attempt to lead from stall — watch for a scrappy first two furlongs where position-fighting could cause interference to horses immediately behind them, particularly Tokyo Treasure and Thenandnow who want to be prominent.

Cool Azul steps up from 6f to 7½f for the first time — if the pace is truly relentless, watch whether he can sustain his effort past the 2f pole; if he stops abruptly, he becomes a serious physical hazard for closers coming through.

Mercurial has been off the track for 79 days and is a natural prominent racer who will struggle to find his position in a field of 18 with three confirmed front-runners already present — watch for an unsettled early passage that could ruin his race before the straight.

Summer Island is only nine days from a run and Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride — in a race where hold-up horses will need a clear run through the final furlong, watch whether McMonagle can thread through or will need to go wide, as Roscommon's straight is narrow for a big field.

The three Reserve jockeys on Mercurial, Java Wood, and Flaming Rib are unknown quantities in a race with a congested early pace — watch how they settle their mounts in the first two furlongs, as inexperienced handling in a pace-heavy 18-runner could compromise the runs of legitimate fancied horses around them.

races.name: District Speciality Coffee Maiden

runners_data.name: Ben Lomond
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran with a 337-day absence and a form string showing minor placing at 2m on Good, but his true hold-up style is squeezed further forward by the weight of backmarkers in this field, and the long layoff is a significant concern at this level.

runners_data.name: Sea Celia's Star
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag who has managed only two runs, the latest 59 days ago on Soft; has not shown ability to sustain her effort and the Good ground, while not a concern, does not solve that pattern.

runners_data.name: Sunny South West
runners_data.note: Consistent six-year-old handicapper who has placed in nine of her last ten starts including twice at this exact 1m4f trip; wears a hood, Jack Cleary takes the ride, and Edward Power's runner has been kept busy with a 20-day turnaround that suggests she is in good order.

runners_data.name: Almazann
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's three-year-old has placed on both career starts at 1m2f and 1m on Good, showing a tidy prominent style that slots neatly behind a single uncontested leader; the step to 1m4f looks a logical progression and the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 1/17 is modest but the horse's profile is the most compelling in the field.

runners_data.name: Daily Wonder
runners_data.note: Debut runner for T G McCourt with no form data, no going profile, and no last-run date available; treated as a complete unknown and the style assessment is similarly blank — no meaningful pace-map role can be assigned.

runners_data.name: Magnum Cor
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old finished fourth on debut at 9f on Good and is a genuine hold-up type by nature, but the density of backmarkers in this 16-runner field means he is unlikely to find his preferred position at the rear; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a high-quality booking but the style compromise is real and the debut run at a shorter trip gives limited stamina evidence.

runners_data.name: Michinaga
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's three-year-old ran ninth on debut at 9f on Good 12 days ago and carries a fade-in-finish flag alongside a lightly-raced caution; the jump to 1m4f is a significant ask first time, and the apprentice booking does not add confidence.

runners_data.name: One Cool County
runners_data.note: A hold-up type by nature whose two runs on Good over 10f and 12f both produced mid-division finishes without threat; the redistribution out of his natural rear position is a genuine tactical disadvantage in a field this large, and the 6-day turnaround suggests connections are keen but the horse has not shown any form to justify confidence.

runners_data.name: Purple Bandit
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Jessica Harrington — Shane Foley takes the ride which is a quality signal — and the hood first-time suggests a potential behavioural reason for it; with no form data the style is unknown and this is simply a watch rather than a usable pace-map runner.

runners_data.name: Swing Street
runners_data.note: Richard John O'Brien's three-year-old ran sixth at 10f on Good 57 days ago in his only start; true hold-up profile but sits in midfield on the map by nature rather than redistribution, and the single run provides very limited evidence for a step to 1m4f.

runners_data.name: Teoest
runners_data.note: Jim Bolger's three-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and Declan McDonogh's booking underlines that role will be fulfilled; has placed on neither of two runs, both at 12f, and the key question is whether this maiden ability level allows Teoest to control the pace without the talent to quicken clear if challenged late.

runners_data.name: De Vega Queen
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan's booking for J A Stack's filly is an upgrade in jockey quality, but three runs have produced nothing better than fourth; as a genuine hold-up type forced into a midfield role by the crowded rear of this field, her style fit is compromised and the form offers no evidence of a winning move on Good ground.

runners_data.name: My Girl Jersie
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's three-year-old has a striking recent form string of 999-0 including a last-place finish, and the fade-in-finish tag reflects that pattern clearly; despite being a natural hold-up type, the crowd of backmarkers pushes her forward on the map, and that misalignment compounds what is already a deeply unflattering form profile — the hood switch is noted.

runners_data.name: Possum
runners_data.note: Jessica Harrington's three-year-old ran eighth on debut at 12f on Good 76 days ago and carries a fade-in-finish flag; the layoff is moderate and there is nothing in the single run to suggest confidence, though the trainer's 14-day rate of 2/32 shows the yard is not in peak form.

runners_data.name: Salamina
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old has recorded two eleventh-place finishes at 10f on Good including a run just four days ago; the very quick turnaround is notable but the form is consistently poor and the fade-in-finish flag is fully supported by both results.

runners_data.name: Venerini
runners_data.note: Michael Butler's three-year-old ran eighth and tenth on her two starts over shorter trips on Good and Soft, with a 105-day break since; the fade-in-finish flag, the absence, and the step up to 1m4f without evidence of staying ability combine to make her profile among the most difficult to assess positively in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Teoest is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner maiden and, crucially, faces no identified challenger for the lead, meaning Declan McDonogh can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout the 1m4f trip on Good ground at Roscommon. With no pressure from behind to force the pace up early, Teoest is likely to set an even, measured tempo that keeps the race relatively bunched and plays into the hands of horses who can travel prominently and quicken from a handy position in the straight. The field contains a significant number of true hold-up types — One Cool County, My Girl Jersie, Magnum Cor, De Vega Queen, and others — who are unlikely to get their natural rear position given the volume of backmarkers competing for the same ground, potentially forcing some of them to race closer than ideal. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just behind a single uncontested leader and produce their effort without cover being stripped away, with Almazann and Sunny South West the clearest beneficiaries of that profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Teoest Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Teoest leads comfortably at a fair gallop and prominent runners travel into the straight without burning fuel chasing.
scenarios.body: Teoest sets a measured pace that compresses the field and allows the two or three horses sitting just behind to strike from an ideal position in the final two furlongs; Good ground rewards those who travel smoothly rather than those forced to make up ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Teoest Leads and Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Teoest's controlled front-running tempo is slow enough that no rival can generate a decisive finishing move.
scenarios.body: With a single leader setting a comfortable pace and no genuine closer able to produce a sprint finish from deep, Teoest's energy reserves remain intact and the front-runner simply outstays all challengers in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo proves even slower than expected and the race turns into a sprint finish that disadvantages horses too close to a non-stayer.
scenarios.body: A dawdle early compresses the field to such a degree that the eventual result is decided by raw finishing speed over the final furlong; runners tagged as redistributed hold-up types who manage to settle away from the scrimmage mid-race could benefit if they find clear daylight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test, Form Horses Flattered
scenarios.trigger: If a pace injection somewhere in the race stretches the field and turns it into a gruelling stamina contest at 1m4f on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Runners with proven staying form over a mile-plus on Good ground come into their own while lightly raced or front-running types who have not proven the trip find the final climb beyond them; Sunny South West's repeated placed efforts at this sort of distance become highly relevant.

watchPoints.text: Almazann's stall draw and early positioning will be critical — if Chris Hayes can sit second or third on the rail behind Teoest from the outset, this horse's prominent style is perfectly suited to the expected pace shape and a forward move turning for home should be anticipated.

Teoest's pace judgement is the fulcrum of the entire race; if Declan McDonogh allows too slow a tempo in the early stages the race could turn into a sprint finish that undermines the front-runner's chance and opens the door for any horse that can quicken off a slow pace.

The volume of hold-up types attempting to race from the rear creates significant crowding risk in the early and middle stages — One Cool County, Magnum Cor, My Girl Jersie, and De Vega Queen cannot all get their natural position, and the resulting jostling mid-race could compromise several runners' chances simultaneously.

Daily Wonder and Purple Bandit are both debut runners from capable yards — Harrington and McCourt — and debut runners in 16-horse maidens can set their own prices if they happen to be well forward on ability; monitor the market move for either in the final minutes before the off.

Sunny South West's hood and consistent placing record at exactly this sort of distance makes her a pace-map fit worth tracking in running — if the prominent horses travel well to the two-furlong pole, she is the one most likely to sustain her effort all the way to the line based on proven staying form.

races.name: Class Grass Handicap

runners_data.name: Catherine Magennis
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed twice over Good ground at 12f-13f recently; Seamie Heffernan adds significant jockey quality and she is well-suited to tracking Out On Friday's uncontested lead with an attacking ride from the front of the chasing pack.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Leggagh
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer who has a single win from 15 Good-ground starts; Hannah Rafferty's 10lb claim helps at the weights and he landed his only win over 12f on Soft, making the step to 1m4f on Good a mild concern, though he has placed at similar trips.

runners_data.name: Daonethatgotaway
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type whose form figures include a recent second at 12f on Standard and a fourth at 12f on Standard; the tongue-tie and hood combination is noted, and the 7lb claiming rider Reese Holohan may struggle to get him into an ideal position in this traffic.

runners_data.name: Deralo Ir
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who has finished second twice on Soft over shorter trips; Robbie Colgan takes the ride but recent Good-ground form shows a 16th and a 7th, and stepping up to 1m4f for the first time on the evidence here looks ambitious.

runners_data.name: Lady Plimsoll
runners_data.note: Hold-up by natural inclination, she has posted two thirds and a second in recent runs across varying trips; trainer O'Callaghan sends her here in good form (T14: 2/14) and the step up to 1m4f suits on pedigree, making her one of the more interesting prospects if she can race closer than her default style suggests.

runners_data.name: Enchanted Lady
runners_data.note: Has raced over shorter trips consistently and is a genuine rear-of-field operator by preference; with four winners from 19 runners in 14 days, trainer A Oliver is in form, but Enchanted Lady is shuffled into a midfield mapping that does not reflect how she will actually race — her STYLE_FIT of 0.92 flags that her chance is materially compromised by this race's shape.

runners_data.name: Summer Snow
runners_data.note: Primarily a shorter-trip performer whose recent runs have been over 7f-8f on Good ground with modest results; stepping up dramatically to 1m4f is a significant ask, and a tongue-tie is applied as the trainer sends her out just 11 days after her last run.

runners_data.name: Double Indian
runners_data.note: A hold-up type who fades in the finish and whose last four runs have all been on Good ground without placing; mapped to midfield out of role with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90, and the consistent pattern of fading late makes this trip a concern rather than a solution.

runners_data.name: Coulstys Way
runners_data.note: Has placed three times over 14f including a third on Good at Roscommon course, which is directly relevant; the 3lb claim of Jack Kearney helps at the weights, and while a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield mapping, the course form is the most compelling asset in her profile.

runners_data.name: Lily Parr
runners_data.note: Has finished in the frame twice over 12f and four times overall in recent runs; Siobhan Rutledge takes the ride and she is a genuine hold-up performer whose natural style is compressed by the excess of closers in this field — the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.90 is honest about her positioning risk.

runners_data.name: Master Sydney
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer who has placed once from 14 Good-ground starts and has run well over extreme trips of 18f-19f; the move back to 1m4f makes tactical sense, though a pacemaker's presence means he cannot rely on a truly strong gallop to aid his late run, and his midfield mapping is out of role.

runners_data.name: Out On Friday
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the field; at ten years old he posts his best performances when allowed to lead unopposed, and 1m4f on Good at Roscommon is the ideal canvas — his ability to control tempo from the outset is the defining tactical factor in this race.

runners_data.name: Spy
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer who has won twice from 15 Good-ground runs and who has produced strong efforts at 16f-17f; the visor is applied and C Byrnes sends him in good enough condition, but mapped to midfield out of true role with STYLE_FIT 0.92, and his best form has come at longer trips than today's 1m4f.

runners_data.name: Chopsticks
runners_data.note: Has placed at 12f on Good and on Standard ground with reasonable consistency; trainer McConnell is operating at T14 3/28, the tongue-tie and hood combination are retained, and while mapped to midfield out of role, his form profile is not without merit in a field of this rating level.

runners_data.name: Fianna
runners_data.note: Returns from a 118-day absence which is a notable flag; has finished third over 12f on Good and placed at similar trips, and tongue-tie plus hood are applied, but the long lay-off combined with being a hold-up type in an unfavourable pace shape creates dual concerns.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Has won over 9f on Good ground and placed at 10f; the step up to 1m4f is a significant trip question for a horse whose recent form is over sprint-to-mile distances, and while mapped to midfield out of true hold-up role, the stamina query is the primary issue here.

runners_data.name: Autocrat
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish as a flagged tendency; form figures include a win over 13f on Good and multiple weak efforts, and the tongue-tie plus breastplate combination does not disguise that this horse's recent record — 17th, 10th, 16th — is deeply uninspiring on Good ground at this sort of trip.

runners_data.name: Piatra Neamt
runners_data.note: Also tagged as a finisher who fades; has been beaten out of sight in several recent Good-ground starts and the pattern of 8th, 14th, 15th, 18th over similar distances is a serious concern regardless of pace shape — the tongue-tie is retained but the evidence of recent form is discouraging.

races.paceDynamic: Out On Friday is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field over 1m4f at Roscommon on Good turf, and with no genuine rival for the lead, this veteran of ten years can dictate a completely uncontested, controlled tempo from the front. At this trip on a flat course in Good conditions, a lone leader setting a sustainable gallop creates a race that strongly favours horses racing prominently — those who can settle just off the pace, save ground, and pick up without needing a sustained finishing burst. Catherine Magennis is the clearest prominent-style runner able to capitalise, with Lady Plimsoll and Duke Of Leggagh also capable of racing handily if they overcome their hold-up tendencies. The field contains a significant excess of natural hold-up horses — Enchanted Lady, Double Indian, Lily Parr, Coulstys Way, Master Sydney and several others are genuine closers who cannot all find their preferred rearward position and are mapped to midfield out of necessity, meaning their true finishing effectiveness is compromised. This race shape emphatically favours horses racing in the top half of the field — prominent-to-mid movers who travel into the race early — because Out On Friday's uncontested lead will not generate the strong pace that true hold-up performers need to come from behind and reel the leaders in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Out On Friday Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Out On Friday leads at a measured tempo with no challenger and the pace never truly quickens, allowing riders tracking close to conserve energy.
scenarios.body: Out On Friday sets a comfortable, sustainable gallop the entire trip and the race becomes a test of who has tracked closest and responds first in the home straight; horses who travelled prominently into the race have a decisive positional advantage over closers stranded in a slowly-strung-out field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Movers Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If a modestly-paced but honest gallop sees two or three prominent horses race into contention turning in and the leader weakens, triggering a straight-line battle among those who tracked second to fourth.
scenarios.body: Catherine Magennis and Lady Plimsoll, having covered the ground efficiently just behind Out On Friday, hit the front inside the final two furlongs and grind it out; the relatively flat Roscommon track rewards those with staying power over outright pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the field compresses late, creating enough momentum for genuine closers to close ground in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Horses redistributed to midfield out of necessity — Enchanted Lady, Lily Parr, or Double Indian — could theoretically benefit if the race develops on terms that suit late-runners, but their out-of-role mapping and low STYLE_FIT scores mean this is a lower-probability outcome; the pace dynamics make it structurally unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Out On Friday's controlled lead proves impossible to reel in and the horse simply outstays an 18-runner field that splits wide and never fully organises.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied early, Out On Friday could simply coast home as the large field falls into disarray behind and fails to mount a coordinated challenge; at OR 62 this requires a career-best effort but the conditions are ideal for such an outcome.

watchPoints.text: Out On Friday (Wesley Joyce) controls the entire shape of this race — watch how quickly he establishes the lead from the stalls; if he is allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the first two furlongs, Catherine Magennis and Lady Plimsoll must be prominent enough to give chase or risk being left with too much to do.

The 18-runner field creates significant traffic risk in the first half-mile at Roscommon, and hold-up horses mapped to midfield out of role — particularly Enchanted Lady, Lily Parr and Coulstys Way — may find themselves unable to travel at their natural rhythm, degrading their effectiveness further than the STYLE_FIT scores alone suggest.

Fianna returns from a 118-day absence — watch market moves and early positioning closely; a horse returning fresh over 1m4f with headgear applied after nearly four months off carries significant fitness uncertainty regardless of previous form.

Lady Plimsoll's trainer O'Callaghan is striking at 2/14 over the past fortnight and she placed at 14f and 16f in recent runs — if Jamie Powell elects to ride closer to the pace than her hold-up tag suggests, she could prove far more dangerous than her natural style implies and would be the most interesting positional watch in the race.

Coulstys Way has the most directly relevant course-and-distance form of any hold-up runner in the field, having placed at 14f at Roscommon on Good — Jack Kearney (3lb claim) gives her a small weight advantage, and if the pace is moderate enough for midfield horses to close, she is the redistribution runner with the strongest credentials.
